scoring_convention: Absence of disclosure scores 2, never 1. No subdimension here scores 1 and none rests on absence of disclosure. Every movement is backed by Human Rights Watch field documentation with named locations, dated events and counted populations. This is a conduct assessment, not a de-seeding.
key_evidence: Human Rights Watch documented on 21 August 2026 that thousands of people had been in the streets of Ceuta 'in a legal vacuum, exposed to sexual violence and without adequate shelter, food, or sanitation for almost three weeks'.

Between 1,385 and 2,168 unaccompanied children were among those unsheltered; 700-750 women were held in open-air sports facilities; over 1,000 men and boys lived in makeshift huts on Trampolin beach; hundreds slept on cardboard in warehouse districts.

The Spanish Interior and Inclusion ministries announced tent camps on 17 August 2026 — eighteen days after the 30-31 July crossing. HRW found the provision fell short of need. This mitigating fact is scored, and is why Boundaries, Accountability, Systemic Thinking and Integrity move only 0.1-0.2.

SCANNER CORRECTION: the scan recorded 'about 1,500 arrivals July 20-29'. HRW documents a mass crossing on 30-31 July 2026, with the Spanish Interior Minister saying 5,000 remain and local organisations estimating up to 10,000. The scan understated the scale and mis-dated the crossing by about ten days.

ATTRIBUTION: the migration event itself is not scored against Spain. HRW states both Spanish central authorities and the Ceuta local government share responsibility; only the national-government share is scored, because Spain sits in the countries index.
The movement is FULLY LINEAR — all eight dimensions were already below 4.0 at the published values, so the integration premium was already zero. No formula threshold effect contributes to the -9.4.

anti_false_positive_screening.baseline_provenance: Published 60.0 was applied on 2026-05-04 from proposal spain-2026-05-02.json (60.9 to 60.0, -0.9). Spain was re-assessed on 2026-07-31, which produced 58.1 and a CONFIRM with no proposal. Verified by reading research/assessments/spain-2026-07-31.subdims.json and research/APPLIED_CHANGES.md. The baseline is recent and evidence-based.
anti_false_positive_screening.no_stale_baseline_rationale: This proposal does not rest on the baseline being old. It rests on a HRW field investigation dated 21 August 2026 documenting conditions that arose after 30 July 2026 — entirely after the 31 July assessment.
anti_false_positive_screening.directionality: Surfaced on negative within-window evidence; proposal is a downgrade. Consistent.
anti_false_positive_screening.not_calibration: Conduct assessment. No peer-calibration argument is used.
anti_false_positive_screening.mitigating_evidence_scored: The 17 August ministerial tent-camp decision is scored upward at AB2 and AC4 and is stated in the report and in key_evidence, so the downgrade cannot be read as ignoring Spain's response.
anti_false_positive_screening.no_formula_artefact: All eight published dimensions were already below 4.0, so the integration premium was already zero. The -9.4 is fully linear.

band_change_evidence_test.reason: No band crossing: Functional at both published (60.0) and proposed (50.6).

notes: Filed under the magnitude trigger (delta -9.4). No band change. Confidence is medium, not high, for one specific reason a reviewer should weigh: the entire adverse finding rests on a single named international rights organisation's field documentation (HRW, tier 3), corroborated on date and substance by one general news source (tier 2). NO tier-4-or-above source — no UN body, EU institution or court finding — was located on the Ceuta situation. Had this been a band crossing it would have failed the evidence test; it is not, so the magnitude trigger applies on its own terms. The mitigating fact that Spain's Interior and Inclusion ministries did act on 17 August 2026 is scored and disclosed.
